The consequence the executor themselves accepts in binding_refusal_B3 ('no W06-01 check may be marked PASS through the registered path until the key is bound; the ids are proven by direct pinned-Go runs only') is therefore accurate, and it caps this card at a blocked recording.

Until that PASS receipt exists under an owner commit, this card can at most be recorded ACCEPT_BLOCKED_RECORDING with unlock = the two owner edits above.

No id anywhere in the selector even names the message - grep for 'output provenance or isolation' across internal/domain/*_test.go returns nothing, and the only ISOLATION-labelled id in expected.json is A03-02-PROJECT-ISOLATION (tenant isolation, a different predicate).
new_risk_scan_dropped_isolation_row.does_it_matter_for_W06_01_NEGATIVE: Not for the three masking faces the NEGATIVE text names, so it is not a blocker on the card's own wording. It DOES matter for the card's deliverable 1 ('the acceptance chain uses a real service transaction'), because :208 is the guard that stops a verifier accepting a run whose output vector contains a verifier-only artifact, and the row was dropped for a reason the code contradicts: the loop at :203 walks the TASK's outputs, so the :222 vector-equality check the executor feared cannot fire first. VERIFIER_ONLY artifacts are constructed in this very package's fixtures (context_test.go:409, domain_test.go:479, backup_upgrade_test.go:299) and one UPDATE of access_class on a sealed output would have reached :208 - the same injection technique part C used for run status and part D used for conflicts. So: recoverable in scope, and cheap.
new_risk_scan_dropped_isolation_row.disposition: OBLIGATION O-2, not a blocker by itself; but the dropped row's stated justification must be corrected rather than left as a design decision.

limitations: I verified the executor's affirmative claims by running their own anchors; I did not audit guards outside the acceptance re-check set. The matrix's own completeness_statement draws that boundary explicitly ('goal acceptance, qualification-plan binding, artifact sealing/use, dispatch admission and native proof paths are not covered by this card's assertions and were not mutated') and I agree it is honest.

V4's survivor reason ('no reachable injection changes the hash without tripping a named guard first') is a coverage argument I could neither prove nor disprove: my drop reproduces survival and my force-probe shows the guard is live, but constructing a discriminating injection would need a new fixture, which this review is not permitted to commit.

The V3a and ISO faces are established as unfalsified by mutation; whether a specific fixture would reach :180's basis clause or :208's isolation clause end-to-end is inferred from the code (frozen schema enum, loop order at :203/:208/:222, artifact_uses.go:100-116) rather than from a test I ran, because I may not add tests. If a future fixture discovers an earlier refusal, the disposition becomes 'survivor with reason plus obligation', which is exactly what the matrix should have recorded in the first place.
Three gate attempts (115/115, 115/115, 115/115) are not enough to characterise the dispatch-fixture flake; they only show it is not deterministic on this machine right now.
The round-1 review file is untracked, so its byte-immutability is supported by mtime-equals-checked_at and by the clean git status of the directory rather than by a git blob comparison.

Mutation runs where a refusal is forced abort a test before it emits (rows 112/114/58/37/1 out of 115); I counted the emitted non-PASS ids and the missing count separately and classified on the non-PASS set, matching the runner's own rule, but a forced-refusal probe is a reachability signal rather than a clean falsifier.

I ran no server, no live resource and no product path: everything measured is DEVELOPMENT/FIXTURE inside the pinned Go 1.27.1 package, so nothing here bears on LIVE qualification or on W06-G02's missing codex.exe resource.
Two mutation attempts crashed my own patch (Go treats an 'if false {' body as no use of a variable) and are reported as crashed, not silently dropped.
